rule.sl:
**will have** + deležnik pove, kaj bo do nekega časa že narejeno: **By Friday I'll have finished the gate.** (Do petka bom {m:končal|f:končala} vrata.) Zanikano **won't have**, vprašanje **Will you have finished by six?**

**by** pove zadnji trenutek: **by Friday**, **by then**, **by the time** + sedanjik: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** (Ko boš {m:prišel|f:prišla}, bomo že pojedli.) Slovenščina reče tu prihodnjik, angleščina sedanjik. **until** pove, do kdaj traja: **I'll work until six.** Slovensko *do* je oboje.

**will have been** + -ing pove, kako dolgo že takrat: **In June I'll have been living here for ten years.**

**will be** + -ing je to, kar se bo ravno dogajalo: **At six I'll be cooking.** Za razliko: **By six I'll have cooked.**

Pove tudi domnevo o zdaj: **Jack will have got home by now.** (Jack je zdaj gotovo že doma.)

V govoru **I'll've**, zato ljudje pišejo tudi *I'll of*. Pisno velja **I'll have**.
rule.de:
**will have** + Partizip sagt, was bis zu einem Zeitpunkt fertig sein wird: **By Friday I'll have finished the gate.** (Bis Freitag werde ich das Tor fertig haben.) Verneint **won't have**, die Frage **Will you have finished by six?**

**by** sagt den letzten Moment: **by Friday**, **by then**, **by the time** + Präsens: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** (Bis du kommst, haben wir schon gegessen.) **until** sagt, wie lange es dauert: **I'll work until six.** Deutsch *bis* ist beides.

**will have been** + -ing sagt, wie lange dann schon: **In June I'll have been living here for ten years.**

**will be** + -ing ist, was genau dann im Gang ist: **At six I'll be cooking.** Der Unterschied: **By six I'll have cooked.**

Es sagt auch eine Vermutung über jetzt: **Jack will have got home by now.** (Jack wird jetzt schon daheim sein.)

Gesprochen **I'll've**, darum schreibt man auch *I'll of*. Geschrieben gilt **I'll have**.
rule.it:
**will have** + participio dice che cosa sarà fatto entro un certo momento: **By Friday I'll have finished the gate.** (Entro venerdì avrò finito il cancello.) Al negativo **won't have**, la domanda **Will you have finished by six?**

**by** dice il termine: **by Friday**, **by then**, **by the time** + presente: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** (Quando arriverai, avremo già mangiato.) L'italiano qui dice il futuro, l'inglese il presente. **until** dice fino a quando: **I'll work until six.** L'italiano distingue *entro* e *fino a*.

**will have been** + -ing dice da quanto tempo, allora: **In June I'll have been living here for ten years.**

**will be** + -ing è ciò che sarà in corso proprio allora: **At six I'll be cooking.** La differenza: **By six I'll have cooked.**

Dice anche un'ipotesi su adesso: **Jack will have got home by now.** (Jack sarà già a casa.)

A voce **I'll've**, perciò si scrive anche *I'll of*. Per iscritto vale **I'll have**.
rule.en:
**will have** + the participle says what will be done by a certain time: **By Friday I'll have finished the gate.** With not **won't have**, to ask **Will you have finished by six?**

**by** says the last moment: **by Friday**, **by then**, **by the time** + the present: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** **until** says how long it goes on: **I'll work until six.**

**will have been** + -ing says how long, by then: **In June I'll have been living here for ten years.**

**will be** + -ing is what will be going on at that moment: **At six I'll be cooking.** The difference: **By six I'll have cooked.**

It also says what you suppose about now: **Jack will have got home by now.**

In talk it's **I'll've**, so people also write *I'll of*. Writing wants **I'll have**.

rule.sl: Do nekega časa narejeno: **will have** + deležnik: **By Friday I'll have finished.** Po **by the time** sedanjik: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** Kako dolgo že: **will have been** + -ing. **by** je najpozneje takrat, **until** do kdaj traja.
rule.de: Bis dahin fertig: **will have** + Partizip: **By Friday I'll have finished.** Nach **by the time** das Präsens: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** Wie lange dann schon: **will have been** + -ing. **by** ist spätestens dann, **until** wie lange es dauert.
rule.it: Fatto entro allora: **will have** + participio: **By Friday I'll have finished.** Dopo **by the time** il presente: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** Da quanto tempo: **will have been** + -ing. **by** è il termine, **until** fino a quando.
rule.en: Done by then: **will have** + the participle: **By Friday I'll have finished.** After **by the time**, the present: **By the time you get here, we'll have eaten.** How long by then: **will have been** + -ing. **by** is the last moment, **until** how long it goes on.

examples.en: By noon Mrs Birkett will have baked the scones.
examples.sl: Do poldneva bo Mrs Birkett spekla sconese.
examples.de: Bis Mittag wird Mrs Birkett die Scones gebacken haben.
examples.it: Entro mezzogiorno Mrs Birkett avrà sfornato gli scone.

examples.en: Next year Arthur will have been keeping bees for fifty years.
examples.sl: Naslednje leto bo Arthur čebelaril že petdeset let.
examples.de: Nächstes Jahr hält Arthur schon fünfzig Jahre Bienen.
examples.it: Il prossimo anno Arthur terrà api da cinquant'anni.

tip.sl: 💡 Slovensko *ko boš prišel* je **when you get here**, *do petka* je **by Friday** ali **until Friday**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch *bis Freitag* ist **by Friday** (fertig) oder **until Friday** (dauert).
tip.it: 💡 *Quando arriverai* è **when you get here**; *entro venerdì* è **by Friday**, *fino a venerdì* **until Friday**.
tip.en: 💡 **by** is the last moment, **until** how long it goes on: **finish by six**, **wait until six**.
